title: 22 demands a ParseError for `__LINE__, which §10.7 requires to expand
detail: VERIFIED: docs/VAMS-LRM/ch10-directives.html has §10.7 ('`__LINE__ expands to the current input line number, in the form of a simple decimal number'); it is a positive requirement with no prohibition anywhere in the clause. The fixture is `//! reject ParseError`, so a CONFORMING compiler compiles the file and FAILS the suite, while a compiler that has never heard of `__LINE__ passes. VerA emits E0114 'unsupported compiler directive' (preprocessor.zig:635-636, unit-tested at 1446) — an implementation state, not a language rule. §10.7 is the one directive rule in the chapter with a hard integer oracle: the physical 1-based line index, counted by the author. Rename off '_unsupported' (the name encodes VerA's schedule). Drop the sidecar and the `// EXPECT: error` line in the same edit.
expected: //! lrm 10.7 + //! print none; body $display("line=%d", `__LINE__) and `CHECKI("`__LINE__ is the physical line number", `__LINE__, <literal line index of that CHECKI line>) plus `CHECKX("branch potential", V(p,n), 0.5) at //! bias V(p)=0.75,V(n)=0.25. Expect a hard FAIL until E0114 is retired for `__LINE__ — that FAIL is the conformance bug, and //! xfail does not apply (README: xfail is only legal next to //! reject).

title: 21 demands a ParseError for `__FILE__, which §10.7 requires to expand
detail: Same inversion as ch10-01: §10.7 says '`__FILE__ expands to the name of the current input file, in the form of a string literal.' No prohibition exists. §10.7 also says the path 'may be implementation dependent', so the pinnable claim is narrower than for `__LINE__: the macro expands, it is a string literal, and %s consumes it. Carry one independent numeric assertion so the fixture is not unasserted (torture reports unasserted fixtures and --strict FAILs them). VerA: E0114, preprocessor.zig:1445.
expected: //! lrm 10.7 + //! print none + //! bias V(p)=0.75,V(n)=0.25; $display("file=%s", `__FILE__); `CHECKX("branch potential", V(p,n), 0.5). Hard FAIL until §10.7 is implemented.

title: 20 pins a `resetall rule chapter 10 never states — a conforming compiler that keeps macros FAILS it
detail: VERIFIED against the HTML: the only two mentions of `resetall in chapter 10 are the §10.1 support table (tagged '[IEEE Std 1364 Verilog]') and §10.2's 'In addition to `resetall, if this directive is used without a discipline name, discipline resolution will not use a default discipline'. Nothing says `resetall undefines a text macro. Whether it does is contested across tools, so the suite is punishing a defensible implementation on an uncitable claim. Also weak-oracle: `//! reject ParseError` is a phase label matched by any parse failure, while VerA's own preprocessor unit test (preprocessor.zig:1426, which names this fixture) asserts E0115.
expected: Either (a) keep as a 1364 fixture: //! lrm 10.1 + //! reject E0115 + a header line quoting IEEE Std 1364 §19.6 verbatim with its clause number; or (b) delete it and let ch10-08 (`resetall clears the DEFAULT DISCIPLINE) carry the chapter's actual `resetall rule. Do not keep an expectation this chapter cannot cite. Drop the sidecar and `// EXPECT: error` either way.

title: §10.4 '`undef shall have no effect on predefined Verilog-AMS macros' — untested, and it passes today
detail: The chapter's cheapest real conformance win. §10.4: 'The `undef compiler directive shall have no effect on predefined Verilog-AMS macros', reinforced by §10.5's 'shall always be defined during the parsing of Verilog-AMS source text'. 13 checks only a virgin stream, 08 checks `undef on a USER macro; nothing crosses them. The naive implementation (one macro table, uniform `undef) silently violates it. VERIFIED VerA already gets it right (preprocessor.zig:181 .predefined flag, 589-591 early return, unit test 1418) and I compiled the proposed body — it passes as written, so the fixture locks in behaviour rather than recording a gap. The 'may issue a warning' half is optional and must not be asserted.
expected: Runnable. //! lrm 10.4 + //! lrm 10.5, //! bias V(p)=0.75,V(n)=0.25; `undef __VAMS_ENABLE__ before the module, witness real live set 1.0 in the `ifdef arm and 2.0 in the `else, `CHECKX("`undef cannot undefine a predefined macro", live, 1.0). Add a `resetall variant of the same witness in the same file.

title: §10.6 'can only be specified outside of a design element' — the chapter's strongest prohibition, zero fixtures
detail: All five keyword fixtures (16, 17, 25, 26, 27) use the legal placement. VERIFIED by running VerA: `begin_keywords inside a module gives error[E0202] 'directive is only legal outside a design element: `begin_keywords inside a module' (parser.zig:310-317, unit test 2237-2243). No xfail needed — it passes on day one. Worth a second body in the same file, or a sibling, for `end_keywords inside a module, since one parser arm handles both tags and a regression could split them.
expected: //! lrm 10.6 + //! reject E0202

title: §10.3's only numeric content — the transition_time the directive sets — is never applied to any filter
detail: 03's own header: 'The 1 ns itself is deliberately NOT pinned', and what it does assert is §4.5.8's DC pass-through, which holds with the directive deleted. So a compiler that lexes `default_transition and discards it passes all of §10.3. VERIFIED §4.5.8 in ch4-expressions.html: 'If neither rise_time nor fall_time are specified or are equal to zero (0.0), the rise and fall time default to the value defined by `default_transition', and the filter 'returns a real number which describes a piecewise linear function over time' — so the LRM oracle is the linear ramp out(t)=t/tr. TWO known VerA gaps make this FAIL: the directive is .ignored (preprocessor.zig:90) and codegen implements transition() as a first-order lag, not a ramp (codegen.zig:2790 zTransition + transitionTau). Both failures are genuine conformance bugs, but the §4.5.8 one is not a chapter-10 defect — note it in the header so the FAIL is not mis-triaged. Keep 03 as the DC pass-through case.
expected: //! lrm 10.3 + //! analysis tran + //! time 0, 1n, 2n, 3n, 4n + //! wave V(in) = 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, with `default_transition 4n. Wants 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 at 1n..4n — t/tr with tr=4e-9, every quotient exact in binary64, so `CHECKX.

title: A version_specifier outside the five §10.6 enumerates has no fixture
detail: §10.6 closes the set: 'VAMS-2023' plus '1364-1995', '1364-2001', '1364-2005', 'VAMS-2.3'. Fixtures 16/17/25/26/27 cover all five accepted spellings and nothing covers rejection. VERIFIED by running VerA: `begin_keywords "1800-2017" gives error[E0135] 'unsupported keyword set: `1800-2017`' (parser.zig:165-170, unit test 2226-2228). SystemVerilog's specifier is the right bad value — it is the one a front end most plausibly accepts by accident. Note §10.6 states a closed enumeration rather than an explicit 'shall be an error'; IEEE Std 1364 §19.11 supplies the explicit form. Passes today.
expected: //! lrm 10.6 + //! reject E0135

title: A stray `end_keywords with no matching `begin_keywords has no fixture
detail: 'until the matching `end_keywords directive is encountered' makes the pairing normative; a stray `end_keywords has no set to restore. VERIFIED: VerA emits error[E0136] '`end_keywords without `begin_keywords' (parser.zig:160-162, unit test 2234). Without the fixture, a compiler that silently swallows the unpaired directive — and so silently leaves the wrong keyword set in force for the rest of the stream — passes the whole chapter. Passes today.
expected: //! lrm 10.6 + //! reject E0136

title: A `begin_keywords never closed by `end_keywords has no fixture
detail: The other half of the pairing rule, and the dangerous direction: §10.6 says the set persists 'even across source code file boundaries', so an unterminated `begin_keywords re-keywords every later file. VERIFIED: VerA emits error[E0137] 'unterminated `begin_keywords: missing `end_keywords' at end of parse (parser.zig:134-142, unit test 2232). Passes today.
expected: //! lrm 10.6 + //! reject E0137

title: Nothing observes what happens AFTER `end_keywords — restoration is never tested
detail: 16, 25 and 26 each wrap their ONLY module in the pair, so the file ends immediately after `end_keywords and a no-op `end_keywords passes all three. The discriminator: after the pair closes, the Verilog-AMS set is back, so `sin` is reserved again. VERIFIED by running VerA on exactly this shape — module m1(sin,n) inside `begin_keywords "1364-2005" ... `end_keywords, then module m2(sin,n) outside it — error[E0208] 'expected an identifier: found `sin`' at the m2 port list. Passes today. (A runnable variant calling sin() after the pair does NOT discriminate: VerA resolves math functions by name regardless of the active set.)
expected: //! lrm 10.6 + //! reject E0208

title: The chapter's only 'shall result in an error' is pinned on the bare substring 'sin'
detail: One unit of work: both files carry the identical three-line header, `//! reject sin`, a `// EXPECT: error` line, a duplicated 'LRM 10.6:' prose line and a sidecar. `//! reject sin` is satisfied by ANY diagnostic containing those three letters — including one about the fixture's own module name ch10_begin_keywords_vams. VERIFIED the stable code exists and fires: parser.zig:2205-2213 asserts diag.Code.E0208 with msg 'found `sin`' for exactly this source, and running VerA on 17's body reproduces it. The header's stated reason ('begin_keywords support is landing concurrently and will reword the message') is now false — token.zig specifier_map and parser.zig implement §10.6. No xfail. NOTE for the same pass: the literals lens recommended DELETING 17 on the grounds that §10.6 never defines "VAMS-2023"; that is a false positive (see the dropped list) — 17 is the LRM's own worked example verbatim and must stay.
expected: //! lrm 10.6 + //! reject E0208 in both; delete `//! reject sin`, the `// EXPECT: error` line, the duplicated prose line and both sidecars.

title: 23 pins the phase label ParseError where the stable code E0115 exists, with no cite
detail: `//! reject ParseError` is satisfied by any parse-phase failure — a typo'd keyword elsewhere in the file would pass it. VERIFIED: preprocessor.zig:635-640 emits E0115 'undefined macro', and diag_code.zig:413-419 already carries .lrm = "10.4" for it. README: 'Codes are the preferred form.' The rule is sound (§10.4 delegates `define/`undef to IEEE Std 1364, whose §19.3.1 makes use of an undefined macro illegal), so only the expectation needs strengthening; write the cite as 10.4-by-delegation in the header.
expected: //! lrm 10.4 + //! reject E0115; delete `// EXPECT: error` and the sidecar.

title: §10.4's only unambiguous 'shall not' — macro TEXT beginning with __VAMS_ — has no fixture
detail: 'To avoid conflicts with predefined Verilog-AMS macros (10.5), the `define compiler directive's macro text shall not begin with __VAMS_.' Syntax 10-3 makes macro_text the BODY, so the rule is about the body, not the name. COVERAGE.md files 15 as covering it; 15 is runnable and tests the legal NAME case (see ch10-20). VERIFIED VerA does not police it: preprocessor.zig only protects the two predefined names (line 102 list), so this is reject + xfail. CORRECTION to the weak lens: it proposed `//! reject E0113`, but E0113 is '`undef requires a macro name' (diag_code.zig:386) — a NEW code is needed, so write the xfail reason and pick the code when the check lands.
expected: //! lrm 10.4 + //! reject <new reserved-macro-text code> + //! xfail VerA never inspects macro text for the __VAMS_ prefix. Body: `define MY_ENABLE __VAMS_ENABLE__.

title: The bare `default_discipline withholds the default from later nets — the rule with teeth, untested
detail: §10.2: 'In addition to `resetall, if this directive is used without a discipline name, discipline resolution will not use a default discipline for nets declared after this directive is encountered in the text stream.' 24 issues the bare form and then declares both nets `electrical` explicitly, so it only checks that the reset is not retroactive — its own header says 'The reset itself has no numeric consequence HERE, and deliberately so'. The rule with an observable consequence is the negative: after the bare reset an UNDECLARED net has no discipline, hence no access function, so V() on it must be an error. This is the ONE discriminating §10.2 fixture available (see ch10-21 for why the positive one is not) and it is contract-shaped. VERIFIED VerA has no such diagnostic at all: a module with discipline-less ports compiles clean today, and any declared nature's access function resolves on them (I compiled a custom rotational discipline and Theta()/Tau() on undeclared ports — accepted). Keep 24 as-is for the non-retroactivity claim.
expected: //! lrm 10.2 + //! reject <new no-discipline code> + //! xfail VerA discards `default_discipline (preprocessor.zig:89) and never applies discipline resolution, so it neither supplies nor withholds a default

title: `resetall clearing the default discipline is the only thing chapter 10 says `resetall does — untested
detail: §10.2 opens the reset sentence with 'In addition to `resetall, ...', which makes `resetall the second way to withdraw the default discipline. The chapter's only `resetall fixture (20) tests a macro claim the chapter never makes (ch10-03). Same shape and same xfail reason as ch10-14, with `resetall in place of the bare directive.
expected: //! lrm 10.2 + //! reject <new no-discipline code> + //! xfail VerA never applies a default discipline, so it has none to clear

title: The apostrophe (0x27) must not introduce a directive — untested, and it passes today
detail: §10.1 spends two sentences on the distinction ('This character is called accent grave (ASCII 0x60). It is different from the character ( ' ), which is the apostrophe character (ASCII 0x27)'), which marks it as a confusion the committee expected; §2.6 gives the apostrophe its own job in sized/based literals. No fixture writes 'define where `define belongs. VERIFIED by running VerA on "'define GAIN 3.0": error[E0201] 'construct is not in the supported subset: `invalid token`' — so this is a passing negative, NOT the xfail the lens assumed. Lowest-value of the passing negatives; include it for census completeness.
expected: //! lrm 10.1 + //! reject E0201 (behaviour pinned: the file does not compile and GAIN is not silently defined)

title: A second `default_transition supersedes the first — no fixture has two of them
detail: §10.3: 'the default rise and fall times for a transition filter are derived from the transition_time value of the directive which IMMEDIATELY PRECEDES the transition filter.' A latched-first or last-wins implementation is invisible today. Depends on ch10-06: until `default_transition is retained and §4.5.8 ramps linearly, this FAILs for the same two root causes, so schedule it after.
expected: //! lrm 10.3; one 0->1 step at t=0 sampled at t=2n: the filter after `default_transition 4n reads 0.5 (2/4), the filter after `default_transition 8n reads 0.25 (2/8). Both exact; the factor of exactly 2 between them is the assertion.

title: An explicit rise/fall argument overrides `default_transition — no fixture pairs the two forms
detail: §10.3 scopes the default to filters 'which ... do not have rise time and fall time arguments specified'; §4.5.8 repeats it ('If neither rise_time nor fall_time are specified or are equal to zero (0.0), the rise and fall time default to the value defined by `default_transition'). Nothing catches a directive that stomps explicit arguments, or a default applied unconditionally. One module, one time point, two filters, two numbers. Same dependency as ch10-17.
expected: //! lrm 10.3 + //! lrm 4.5.8; 0->1 step at t=0 sampled at t=2n under `default_transition 8n: transition(x) reads 0.25 (2/8), transition(x, 0, 4n, 4n) reads 0.5 (2/4). Both exact.

title: Nothing tests that a VAMS keyword set is not OVER-broad: §10.6 names `logic` on the permitted side
detail: §10.6's third worked example: 'Note that the word "logic" is not a keyword in Verilog-AMS 2023, whereas it is a keyword in the IEEE Std 1800 SystemVerilog.' It is the counterpart of `sin` on the forbidden side, which 17/27 cover. A compiler built on a SystemVerilog front end — the most plausible real-world implementation — fails this and passes everything else in §10.6. VERIFIED: 'logic' is not in VerA's keyword tables (no match in token.zig) and I compiled `real logic; logic = 2.5;` under `begin_keywords "VAMS-2023" — accepted. Passes today. (The LRM example writes the DISCIPLINE as escaped `\logic`; the plain identifier case is the cheap and unambiguous half.)
expected: Runnable. //! lrm 10.6, //! bias V(p)=0.75,V(n)=0.25; real logic; logic = 2.5; `CHECKX("logic is an ordinary identifier under VAMS-2023", logic*V(p,n), 1.25). 2.5*0.5 is exact.

title: 15 is named and filed for a prohibition it does not test; it asserts acceptance and duplicates 04
detail: VERIFIED the fixture and its literal are CORRECT: §10.4 restricts the macro TEXT, Syntax 10-3 makes text_macro_identifier a plain identifier, so `define __VAMS_USER_FORBIDDEN 7.0 is legal and 7.0*0.5 = 3.5 is exact — do not touch the digits. The defect is the label: the filename says 'reserved_vams_macro_prefix' and COVERAGE.md s10-4 files it as 'forbidden `__VAMS_` prefix nonconformance', so the chapter looks like it covers the prohibition when the prohibition is untested (ch10-13). Fix the prose BEFORE any reject rewrite, so nobody deletes a correct literal on the strength of the wrong label.
expected: Rename to what it proves, add //! lrm 10.4, keep `CHECKX(..., 3.5) verbatim, and correct the COVERAGE.md s10-4 cell (folded into ch10-24).

title: `default_discipline is never applied to an undeclared net — but the obvious fixture cannot fail either
detail: The lens headline is right: 01, 02 and 24 all declare `electrical p, n;` and each header admits the directive is inert ('no value here can depend on it'), so §10.2's whole positive effect is untested. The lenses' proposed fix — drop the discipline declaration and assert V(p,n)==0.5 — does NOT discriminate, VERIFIED: VerA compiles a module whose ports have no discipline at all, and resolves any declared nature's access function on them (a custom rotational discipline with Theta/Tau on undeclared ports compiles clean; only a name that is no access function at all gives E0512). So the proposed fixture passes with the directive deleted — the same defect it was written to remove. Write it only as a spec record, with the header saying plainly what it cannot yet discriminate, and treat the discriminating case as ch10-14. The access-resolution leniency is a separate VerA ticket, not a ch10 fixture.
expected: Runnable, LOW value until discipline resolution exists. //! lrm 10.2, //! bias V(p)=0.75,V(n)=0.25, `default_discipline electrical, ports with NO discipline declaration, `CHECKX("the defaulted net has the electrical potential access", V(p,n), 0.5) — 0.75-0.25 per §1.3.1, exact.

title: Qualifier selection and directive precedence: two defaults in force at once, untested
detail: Merges the qualifier rule and the precedence sentence — one fixture answers both. §10.2: 'more than one `default_discipline directive can be in force simultaneously, provided each differs in qualifier', and 'the more specific directives have higher precedence over general directives'. 02 uses `real` precisely because it matches nothing in the module, so it proves only that the qualifier PARSES. The discriminating shape is two directives and two nets: the `reg`-qualified net takes ddiscrete, the plain net takes electrical; last-wins or first-wins gets exactly one of them wrong. Same caveat as ch10-21 — VerA discards the directive and resolves access regardless, so today it cannot fail; write it as the spec record for when resolution lands.
expected: //! lrm 10.2; `default_discipline electrical wire + `default_discipline ddiscrete reg over nets with no discipline declaration; `CHECKX("the wire-qualified default supplies electrical", V(p,n), 0.5) at V(p)=0.75/V(n)=0.25 (§1.3.1), and `CHECKI on the reg net's discrete value.

title: `__LINE__ remapping by `line and by `include is untested — and only observable once §10.7 exists
detail: Two §10.7 sentences in one fixture: 'An `include directive changes the expansions of `__FILE__ and `__LINE__ ... revert to the values they had before the `include (but `__LINE__ is then incremented by one)' and 'A `line directive (as defined in IEEE Std 1364 Verilog) changes `__LINE__'. 19 already carries `line 100 "virtual.va" 0 purely as a no-op, and COVERAGE.md concedes 'its remapped location is not observable'. The include-revert half is the most error-prone rule in the clause — a preprocessor that splices included text into one flat buffer reports a line number inflated by the length of constants.vams (~95 lines). Depends on ch10-01; also blocked by preprocessor.zig:98 ('`line ... GAP: does not remap `__LINE__'). Split into two files if the derivation gets hard to read.
expected: //! lrm 10.7; after `include "check.vh" two consecutive `CHECKI wants that differ by exactly the physical line gap in the .va and are NOT inflated by the included file's length; after `line 100 "virtual.va" 0, `CHECKI(..., `__LINE__, 100) then 101 — IEEE 1364 §19.7 numbers the line FOLLOWING the directive.

title: COVERAGE.md records VerA's state instead of the rules, and three of its cells are now factually wrong
detail: One pass over the file. (a) s10-4 files 15 as 'forbidden `__VAMS_` prefix nonconformance' — VERIFIED false, 15 asserts the legal name case (ch10-20). (b) s10-6 says 'VerA currently ignores the selected keyword set ... the two VAMS fixtures freeze its invalid acceptance' — VERIFIED false, token.zig specifier_map and parser.zig implement §10.6 and E0208 fires on `sin`. (c) s10-2/s10-3/s10-7 are written as implementation snapshots ('the snapshots prove directive acceptance rather than the resulting discipline state', 'the directive is consumed but its default is not retained', 'neither macro is currently implemented') — each belongs on its fixture as an //! xfail reason or nowhere. (d) Add the §10.3 note: the clause self-contradicts ('it can be used only outside of module definitions' vs 'There are no scope restrictions for this directive', both VERIFIED present in the HTML and the 2.4 PDF), so NEITHER reading is pinned, deliberately. (e) Drop the 'Literal fixture inventory' — it duplicates ls and cannot be kept true.
expected: Each row states the RULE and the fixture that pins it, joined by the //! lrm cite; no 'VerA currently ...' prose.

title: Six abolished sidecars and six `// EXPECT: error` lines still on disk
detail: README opens with 'No sidecar files' and the point of `//! reject` is that 'there is no second file to drift out of step with it'. VERIFIED six sidecars and six `// EXPECT: error` lines (the negatives lens said four). They agree with the in-file lines today, which is exactly the state where one gets edited and the other does not. COUPLING: tests/conformance.zig still reads `<stem>.expected-error.txt` as its oracle (conformance.zig:97-98), so the deletion lands with that runner's retirement, not before. Every 'rewrite'/'edit' item above should drop its own sidecar in the same commit.
expected: rm the six sidecars; delete the six `// EXPECT: error` lines and the duplicated 'LRM 10.6:' prose lines in 17 and 27.

title: Chapter 10 has zero //! lrm cites
detail: VERIFIED: grep finds six `//! reject` lines and not one `//! lrm` in the chapter — under the new contract every reject fixture here is a fixture error. CONTEXT the lenses missed: no chapter has any yet (the only //! lrm in tests/fixtures is the README's example), so this is the suite-wide migration reaching ch10, not a ch10-specific regression. The cites also carry --coverage, which is the only mechanical backing for a 'chapter 10 is covered' claim.
expected: One //! lrm per fixture naming the clause it pins (10.1 for 19/20-as-1364, 10.2 for 01/02/24, 10.3 for 03, 10.4 for 04-08/15/23, 10.5 for 13/14/18, 10.6 for 16/17/25/26/27, 10.7 for 21/22); IEEE-1364-delegated rules cite the ch10 clause that delegates.

title: Four §10.6 diagnostics cite .lrm = "10.2", and E0114 cites §10.7 for §10.1 directives
detail: VERIFIED in diag_code.zig: E0135 (line 597), E0136 (607), E0137 (615) and E0202 (657) all set .lrm = "10.2", and E0202's explain text reads 'LRM 10.2 confines them to the space between design elements' — all four are §10.6 rules; §10.2 is `default_discipline. The four new §10.6 reject fixtures (ch10-05/07/08/09) will cite //! lrm 10.6 while the diagnostic they pin says 10.2, so --coverage and the diagnostic disagree about which clause fired. Separately E0114 carries .lrm = "10.7" and its explain calls `resetall/`timescale/`celldefine 'the remaining LRM 10.7 directives' — those are §10.1 table entries; §10.7 is `__FILE__/`__LINE__, which is also why 21/22 read as language rules instead of gaps.
expected: .lrm = "10.6" on E0135/E0136/E0137/E0202 and the matching explain text; E0114 recited to 10.1 with its explain corrected, or split so `__FILE__/`__LINE__ get their own §10.7 gap code.

title: `unconnected_drive is the one §10.1 directive no fixture writes
detail: VERIFIED: grep over the whole fixture tree matches `unconnected_drive` only inside `nounconnected_drive` in 19 and in COVERAGE.md's own admission ('the decay/strength, delay-mode, protect, and `unconnected_drive directives are absent'). Every other §10.1 entry is written somewhere. preprocessor.zig:95 already maps it to .ignored, so it is a one-line edit and the existing assertions carry the claim.
expected: Add `unconnected_drive pull1 before the module (19 already ends with `nounconnected_drive); the existing `CHECK("the ignored directives leave the branch potential alone", V(p,n), 0.5, 1e-15) is the oracle.

title: 14's `else-arm label names a claim the assertion does not test
detail: The `else arm asserts `CHECKX("without the extensions the model is the plain resistor", 2.0*V(p,n), 1.0) — arithmetic on the bias with no LRM content behind the label. VERIFIED VerA predefines __VAMS_COMPACT_MODELING__ (preprocessor.zig:102-104), so the `else arm is dead text in this build and the ddx digits (+1/-1 from §4.5.6's vccs example) are what actually runs. The lens is right that a simulator supporting every extension but never defining the macro is green here, and right that §10.5 makes that unassertable ('if and only if all the compact modeling extensions are supported'), so the fix is honest labelling, not a new claim. Cosmetic.
expected: Add //! lrm 10.5 and //! lrm 4.5.6; relabel the else arm to what it proves ('the compact-modeling macro is not defined, so the else arm compiled'). Consider moving the ddx digits to an unconditional chapter-4 fixture so §4.5.6 is pinned regardless of the macro.

title: Syntax 10-1's closed qualifier list and Syntax 10-2's mandatory operand are unpoliced
detail: Merged: two BNF-backed prohibitions with the same root cause and the same xfail reason. Syntax 10-1 closes the qualifier alternation at fifteen names, so `default_discipline electrical electrical is a syntax error; Syntax 10-2 makes transition_time mandatory and a constant_expression, so a bare `default_transition is one too. VERIFIED VerA consumes both directives to end of line without parsing them (preprocessor.zig:89-90, .ignored), so it accepts anything — xfail both. Lowest value in the chapter: the failure mode is a typo'd directive silently ignored, and neither fixture can discriminate anything until the preprocessor parses directive operands at all. Two small files if one reads badly.
expected: //! lrm 10.2 / //! lrm 10.3 + //! reject <syntax code> + //! xfail VerA discards the directive text wholesale

title: Syntax 10-3 restricts a macro formal to a simple_identifier; escaped identifiers untested
detail: Syntax 10-3 deliberately distinguishes the two: text_macro_identifier ::= identifier (so an escaped macro NAME is legal) while formal_argument_identifier ::= simple_identifier (so an escaped FORMAL is not). 05 covers the legal simple form. Genuinely marginal, kept for census completeness — and the more useful half is the positive it licenses: an escaped macro NAME, which is also untested and is runnable.
expected: //! lrm 10.4 + //! reject <syntax code> + //! xfail, plus (preferred, cheaper, runnable) the escaped-macro-name positive with an exact literal.
